# Quick Study Guide: 6. Field Modification & In-Place Update Operators (CRUD Update)

> "updateOne(filter, update) updates the first document that matches a query filter, using update operators such as $set to modify specific fields without replacing the whole document. updateMany(filter, update) updates every document that matches a query filter, applying the same update operators to each matching document. $set replaces a field's value; $inc adds to a numeric field; $push/$pull add to or remove from an array field."

## 6.1 Update Scope & Execution Methods

> "updateOne(filter, update) updates the first document that matches a query filter, using update operators such as $set to modify specific fields without replacing the whole document. updateMany(filter, update) updates every document that matches a query filter, applying the same update operators to each matching document."

- **Single-Target Modification (`updateOne(filter, update)`).** `updateOne()` takes two mandatory arguments: `<filter>` (selection criteria) and `<update>` (must contain `$` update operators like `$set`). It modifies only the first matching document and returns `{ acknowledged: true, matchedCount: 1, modifiedCount: 1, upsertedId: null }`.
- **Multi-Target Modification (`updateMany(filter, update)`) & In-Place Preservation.** `updateMany()` applies the `<update>` operators to every document matching `<filter>`. Crucially, both `updateOne()` and `updateMany()` modify only the fields specified inside `$set` (or other `$` operators) without replacing the entire document.

```javascript
// 1. Single-document update (modifies first match only)
db.students.updateOne(
  { name: "Rahul" },
  { $set: { age: 20 } }
);
// Output: { acknowledged: true, matchedCount: 1, modifiedCount: 1, upsertedId: null }

// 2. Multi-document batch update (modifies all matching documents)
db.students.updateMany(
  { age: 18 },
  { $set: { promoted: true } }
);
db.students.updateMany(
  { grade: 8 },
  { $set: { promoted: true } }
);
```

| Feature | `updateOne(filter, update)` | `updateMany(filter, update)` |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Match Cardinality | First matching document only | All matching documents (`1..N`) |
| Second Argument Requirement | Must use `$` operators (`$set`, etc.) | Must use `$` operators (`$set`, etc.) |
| Unreferenced Fields | Preserved untouched | Preserved untouched |
| Return Telemetry | `{ matchedCount: 0\|1, modifiedCount: 0\|1 }` | `{ matchedCount: N, modifiedCount: M }` |

## 6.2 Atomic Field Update Operators

> "$set replaces a field's value; $inc adds to a numeric field; $push/$pull add to or remove from an array field."

- **Scalar Assignment (`$set`) & Atomic Numeric Increment (`$inc`).** `$set` replaces the value of a field (or creates the field if missing) while leaving all other document fields untouched. `$inc` adds a positive or negative numeric delta to a number field atomically (initializing the field to the delta value if missing).
- **Array Mutation (`$push` & `$pull`) & Multi-Operator Composition.** `$push` appends an element to the end of an array field (or creates a 1-element array if missing), while `$pull` removes all instances matching a value from an array. You can combine `$set`, `$inc`, and `$push` inside a single `updateOne()` call.

```javascript
// 1. Atomic multi-operator update combining $set, $inc, and $push
db.students.updateOne(
  { name: "Rahul" },
  {
    $set: { age: 20 },
    $inc: { attempts: 1 },
    $push: { subjects: "History" }
  }
);

// 2. Conditional array element removal using $pull
db.students.updateOne(
  { name: "Rahul" },
  { $pull: { subjects: "Science" } }
);
```

| Operator | Target Field Type | Action on Existing Field | Behavior if Field Is Missing |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `$set` | Any field type | Overwrites field value | Creates field with specified value |
| `$inc` | Numeric (`int`/`double`) | Adds positive/negative delta | Creates field initialized to delta |
| `$push` | Array field | Appends item to end of array | Creates new 1-element array `[item]` |
| `$pull` | Array field | Removes all matching items | No-op (document unchanged) |

---

## Rapid Exam Trap Checklist

- **Trap 1 — Missing `$` Operator in `updateOne()`**: Passing `{ age: 20 }` instead of `{ $set: { age: 20 } }` as the second argument to `updateOne()` throws a `MongoInvalidArgumentError` (update document requires atomic operators).
- **Trap 2 — Behavior on Missing Fields**: If the field targeted by `$set` or `$inc` does not exist in the matched document, MongoDB creates the field automatically; if an array field targeted by `$push` is missing, MongoDB creates a single-element array.
- **Trap 3 — `$pull` Removes All Matches**: Unlike `pop`, `$pull` removes **every** occurrence of the matching value from the target array in a single operation.
